newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut Blue Cross agrees to merge with Anthem.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut Blue Cross agrees to merge with Anthem.

text.p: Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut said Tuesday it tentatively agreed to merge with Indianapolis-based Anthem Inc. to form a multi-regional health insurance company with more than $11.5 billion in revenues.
The proposal to merge the two mutual insurance companies must be approved by insurance commissioners in Connecticut and Indiana as well as the policyholders of both companies.
The merger is scheduled to be finalised next year, Connecticut Blue Cross said. As part of the merger, it will be given two seats on Anthem's board.
Connecticut Blue Cross would become part of Anthem East Inc., based in Newark, N.J., which will serve as Anthem's operations centre on the East Coast.

Connecticut Blue Cross is the state's largest health insurer, serving about 850,000 Connecticut residents. The insurer, which has revenues of $1.5 billion, has been losing customers to managed care companies such as Oxford Health Plans.
Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut provides health care benefits and managed care programmes to about 850,000 Connecticut residents and is the state's largest managed care company.

Anthem East also will administer Blue Cross & Blue Shield of New Jersey, which Anthem agreed to acquire earlier this year. Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Jersey, meanwhile, had previously agreed to acquire the assets of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Delaware.
The Blue Cross & Blue Shield of New Jersey deal is expected to be completed in early 1997, an Anthem spokesman said.

Anthem also controls Blue Cross and Blue Shield franchises in Indiana and Ohio and discount health networks in Florida, California and other states. The Connecticut Blue Cross merger does not involve cash payments.

"This is an exciting opportunity for Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut and undoubtedly, the most dramatic change proposed since the company was founded more than 60 years ago," said Chairman John Croweak.

"It is critical that we seize this opportunity if we are to become bigger, stronger, more competitive and better positioned to survive in the rapidly changing world that is health care today," he said.
Just last week, New York state's Empire Blue Cross & Blue Shield announced plans to convert to a for-profit corporation to better compete with managed-care companies.
Anthem Inc., the parent of insurance broker Acordia Inc., covers more than 9 million people nationwide and had consolidated revenues in 1995 of $7.5 billion.
